clue.text: Stimulate knowledge, you might say

indicators.note: signals that the word for knowledge is to be heard, not spelt, giving its soundalike

parts.note: insight is knowledge or understanding

explanation.surface: A teacher urging that learning should spur the mind on.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate someone is to stir or provoke them into action, a direct synonym.

clue.text: At home, baby's fed to grow

parts.note: in means at home
a cub is a baby animal
ate means fed, took food

explanation.surface: An infant being nourished at home so it can thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs or ideas develop when kept warm or nurtured, so the word means to grow or develop.

clue.text: Prisoner finds hammer in piece of bread

indicators.note: in places the word for hammer within the word for prisoner

parts.note: con is short for convict
to hammer an opponent is to rout them

explanation.surface: An inmate discovers a hammer hidden inside a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammer' looks like a tool smuggled into jail; it means a heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of fried or toasted bread, served in soup or salad.

clue.text: On vacation, throw rocks again?

indicators.note: vacation means emptying, so throw is emptied of its inner letters

parts.note: ice served in a drink is 'on the rocks'

explanation.surface: Asking whether to toss stones once more while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' looks like a holiday; it means emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something again means doing it a second time, so two times; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Pass an examination

definitions.meaning: to pass a car on the road, a British sense of overtake
a thorough inspection and repair of a machine or system

explanation.surface: A student hoping to succeed in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as succeeding in a test; it is the driving sense, going past another vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a driver who overtakes another vehicle is said to do this; it is also a full check-up of machinery.

clue.text: Proof that "I" for "inactive" unravels

indicators.note: unravels means the letters come apart and are rewoven in a new order

explanation.surface: A grammatical point: swapping one word for another is shown to fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Confirmation that something is true or accurate is proof of it.

clue.text: Palm tree fences mostly to prevent parasitic plants

definitions.note: Rafflesia is a genus, so the name covers several plants

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the palm goes around the other piece

parts.note: raffia is a palm tree whose fibre is used for weaving

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: lest means in order to prevent

explanation.surface: Fencing palm trees to keep out parasites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm tree' is one piece, the raffia palm, not a palm plus a tree; 'fences' means surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafflesia is a genus of parasitic flowering plants of South-East Asia, famous for huge foul-smelling blooms.

clue.text: Sussex town seminar — undelivered packages

indicators.note: packages means the letters are wrapped up within the following words

explanation.surface: A seminar in a southern English town where parcels never arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Arundel is a town in West Sussex, a county on England's south coast, known for its castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a historic market town in West Sussex, England.

clue.text: Female can notice dishonesty about this

indicators.note: about means the word for dishonesty goes round the other piece

parts.note: lies are dishonesty
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A woman able to spot deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as 'is able to'; it is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A women's public toilet is called this in Britain; 'can' is American slang for a toilet.

clue.text: Pianist about to be given offer of lift?

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
'hop in' is what a driver says when offering someone a ride

explanation.surface: A pianist about to be offered a ride somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the great Polish-French composer and pianist.

clue.text: Supporting institute is great

parts.note: pro means in favour of
to institute something is to found or establish it

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine institution that backs you.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means very great or intense, as in profound relief or profound ignorance.

clue.text: Psychology exercise trap?

parts.note: a role is a part, and reversing the word part gives the clue word trap

explanation.surface: A psychology test that is really a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: a synonym of role, turned around, gives trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping positions with another person is a technique used in therapy and psychology training.

clue.text: Ms Davis returned for fellow that's richer

parts.note: Bette Davis, the Hollywood film star

indicators.note: returned means the word for is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: Bette Davis comes back for a companion who has more money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a more prosperous position is wealthier; the phrase is an idiom for having more money.

clue.text: Good in bed? You can stay here

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the word for bed

parts.note: a lode is a vein or bed of ore in rock

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast about bedroom prowess followed by an invitation to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good in bed' reads as a saucy compliment; bed is a geological seam of ore.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin or small house where visitors such as hunters or skiers are put up for a time.

clue.text: Can story about posh girl provide role for a ruin?

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: about means the story word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a tale is a story
gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl
to cast an actor is to give them a part

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tale about an upper-class girl could supply a part in a play about a ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintagel Castle is a ruined castle on the Cornish coast linked with King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish clifftop fortress survives only as crumbling remains, so it is a famous example of one.

clue.text: George wants a book, not a collection

indicators.note: not tells us the second a is removed from the book title

parts.note: Utopia is the book by Thomas More
a lot is a collection of items at auction

explanation.surface: A man named George wants a book but not an entire set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' looks like a person; it is RAF slang for the automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George is old pilots' slang for the automatic flight-control system that flies a plane unaided.

clue.text: 3 hilarious stories

indicators.note: refers to the answer to 3 down, which means two times, so the piece is doubled

parts.note: 'a gas' is slang for something hilarious

explanation.surface: A trio of very funny tales.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga saga is a British genre of novel about middle-class country life; an Aga is a range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: These are novels of comfortable English rural middle-class life, so stories of a particular kind.

clue.text: 14's dubious stocktaking activity

indicators.note: dubious means questionable or unreliable, so the letters of the cross-referenced entry are jumbled

parts.note: refers to the answer to 14 across, the Cornish ruin

explanation.surface: A shady practice associated with the ruin from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocktaking' looks like counting goods in a shop; here it is the literal taking of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is the theft of farm animals, a playful reading of taking stock where stock means livestock.

clue.text: Like down, up?

parts.note: as means like
under means below or down

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether down could be the same as up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means broken up, as in torn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart into pieces, as things are when broken or torn up.

clue.text: Publication has gone for litigation

parts.note: has and is can both be written as 's, so one stands for the other
suing is taking legal action

explanation.surface: A newspaper has abandoned its legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of putting out a book or magazine; issuing is the gerund of putting into print.

clue.text: In Paris I try standing up for the rich

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a test is a try

explanation.surface: A visitor in Paris trying to stand up for wealthy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy fashionable people who travel the world are collectively called this.

clue.text: Supply drug — crack

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A dealer providing drugs, including crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a second drug; it is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with what they need, as in kitting out an expedition.

clue.text: Is hiding monster they try to banish

indicators.note: hiding means the first piece covers and contains the second

parts.note: to be is to exist, so is gives exists
an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction

explanation.surface: A monster is concealed somewhere, and certain people try to drive it out.
explanation.definitionFit: These are priests or others who try to drive demons and evil spirits out of people or places.

clue.text: Get painter some coconut

parts.note: to cop is to get or catch
RA, Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Asking an artist for a bit of coconut.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried coconut kernel from which oil is pressed is this product.

clue.text: Swine! Very famous member of fraternity

parts.note: sod is British slang insult for an unpleasant person, like swine
A-list describes the most famous celebrities

explanation.surface: Insulting a celebrated brother of some society.
explanation.walkthrough: SOD is mild British slang for an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sodality is a religious brotherhood or guild, and one belonging to it is a fellow member.

clue.text: Extremely sharp sound makes you jump

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of sharp

parts.note: to ring is to make a sound like a bell

explanation.surface: A sudden piercing noise startles you.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap or bound up suddenly is to jump.

clue.text: Accelerator and choke

definitions.meaning: the device controlling fuel flow to an engine, operated by the pedal
to strangle someone by the throat

explanation.surface: Two car controls named side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like car parts; the second is really to strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: The valve regulating an engine's fuel is this; as a verb it means to strangle.

clue.text: Express grief about eating a good local dish

indicators.note: eating means the reversed piece swallows the others

parts.note: to sigh is to express grief

explanation.surface: Someone mourning while having a decent meal of regional food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SIGH into HGIS before A and G go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's national dish of offal and oatmeal in a casing, local to a Scottish setter's audience.
